sn16.13:1.4: Asked by Bhaddāli at [mn65:29.1](). There, the Buddha said, as he did to Sāriputta at [pli-tv-bu-vb-pj1:3.4.6](), that decline comes from defiling influences in the Saṅgha.
sn16.13:1.8: In an age of commercialized spirituality, AI, the proliferation of sects and gurus, and the collapse of moral authority of traditional Saṅgha under the weight of institutional corruption, this seems relevant.
sn16.13:2.1: _Jātarūpa_ is the natural, unworked gold, for which the technical term is “native gold” (see [an3.70:38.4](), [an3.101:1.1]()). I believe _jātarūpa_ stems from the common Vedic sense of _rūpa_ as “form” or “manifestation” of the gods. _Jāta_ is what is “born” or what is part of the “natural” order. Thus _jātarūpa_ is the manifestation of the divine form (of the sun) in nature.
sn16.13:2.2: Kauṭilya details the regulation of the various kinds of gold and its adulterants in Arthaśāstra 2.13 and 2.14.
sn16.13:3.1: That is to say, there is no objective material cause.
